A.title: When Everyday Meals Become a Cultural Surprise
A.text:
People who move or travel abroad often discover that food is more than a list of ingredients. The time of meals, the way people share dishes and the meaning of politeness can be different. Five travellers describe what surprised them about eating in new places.

A — EMILY: When I arrived in Vietnam, I expected a large breakfast with toast, fruit and tea. Instead, my neighbours invited me for a hot bowl of noodle soup before work. At first I thought soup belonged at lunch. Now I sometimes eat it in the morning because it is filling and convenient. The small local café is busy before seven o’clock.

B — MUSA: In my hometown, family members usually eat from individual plates. During a visit to a friend in Jordan, several dishes were placed in the centre of the table for everyone to share. I was surprised by how often people offered me more food. My friend explained that sharing food was a way of showing care, not an expectation that I should eat everything.

C — SOFIA: I became a vegetarian two years ago. When I travel, I ask about ingredients because vegetable dishes sometimes contain meat stock or fish sauce. In one small restaurant, the chef carefully explained every ingredient and prepared a different sauce for me. I appreciated that flexibility. It made me feel comfortable although I could not read the local menu.

D — JACK: I first tried eating with chopsticks when I travelled to Taiwan. The first few attempts were difficult; I dropped my noodles several times. A friend showed me how to hold the sticks, and I practised every day. Now I can use them for most meals, but I still find small slippery pieces hard to pick up.

E — AMINA: I was taught that people should leave the table soon after finishing a meal. At a dinner with a host family abroad, everyone stayed and talked for an hour after eating. The food was delicious, but the long conversation was even more memorable. I realised that mealtimes can be an important opportunity to maintain friendships.

B.title: Cooking Shows: Learning, Entertainment or Both?
B.text:
Television programmes about cooking have become popular on many platforms. Some teach viewers how to prepare affordable meals at home. Others focus on competition, famous personalities or unusual ingredients. These different formats appeal to different audiences.

A — PRACTICAL LESSONS. A weekly programme called Home Kitchen teaches viewers to prepare simple meals. Each episode shows every stage and explains why ingredients are added. The host often demonstrates a lower-cost alternative for families who want to save money. Viewers can follow a recipe without expensive equipment.

B — THE COOKING CONTEST. In Kitchen Challenge, six amateur cooks prepare dishes under time pressure. The judges discuss taste, appearance and cooking methods. The programme is exciting, but viewers may not learn enough about measurements to repeat the recipes at home. The show is designed mainly to entertain.

C — FAMILY COOKING. In Cook Together, children cook with an adult relative. The emphasis is on safety, cooperation and choosing fresh foods. Young viewers learn that adults should handle hot pans and sharp knives. The programme has encouraged some families to cook together at weekends.

D — FOOD HISTORY. The series Meals Through Time explores dishes from different periods. Historians explain how people stored food before modern refrigerators and how trading routes changed the ingredients available in different regions. The presenters travel to museums and speak with local cooks.

E — PROFESSIONAL IDEAS. In The Restaurant Lab, chefs visit small restaurants and suggest ways to reduce waste. They discuss portion sizes, seasonal vegetables and planning a weekly menu. The programme argues that making food efficiently does not always require buying more products.

F — WHAT VIEWERS DO. Surveys of television audiences suggest that watching a cooking programme does not necessarily mean a person will cook more often. Some people enjoy watching the competition but prefer ready-made meals. Others try one new recipe each month. For learners, a useful first step is to choose a simple recipe, prepare a short shopping list and practise safely with someone experienced.

A.title: A meal for friends
dialogue: What should we cook for our friends on Saturday? I was thinking of fried chicken, but Hannah does not eat meat.
Then how about vegetable noodles? We can boil the noodles and fry the vegetables.
Good idea. But please do not add peanuts. Hannah is allergic to them.
Of course. We could bake a small apple cake for dessert.
I wanted to start cooking at four, but our friends will arrive at six, so let us begin at half past four.
Perfect. I will buy carrots, mushrooms and two packets of noodles.

B.title: At a street-food stall
dialogue: Good afternoon. Are your dumplings fried?
We have fried ones, but our most popular dumplings are steamed.
I would like six steamed dumplings. Are they spicy?
No. We serve the hot sauce separately.
Seven dollars fifty. Actually, it is six fifty today because we have a lunch offer.
Great. And may I have a mango drink with no sugar?
Certainly. I will prepare it fresh.

C.title: Three places to eat
dialogue: Welcome to City Food Radio. Today we are talking about three restaurants. First, Green Garden.
Green Garden serves vegetarian meals. Its vegetable curry is delicious, and the staff are friendly. It is a little expensive though.
River Grill is famous for grilled fish and chicken. It has a lovely view of the river, but the service can be slow on weekends.
Market Bowl is small and inexpensive. Students love its noodle soup. The room is noisy, but the portions are generous.
So you recommend Green Garden for vegetarians, River Grill for a view, and Market Bowl for a low-cost lunch?

D.title: Food in three countries
dialogue: In our travel programme, three visitors describe memorable meals. Wei visited China and tried a bowl of noodle soup with fresh vegetables.
He also learned that people may use chopsticks made from bamboo to pick up food.
Sora visited Japan. She enjoyed rice balls filled with vegetables. Some were wrapped in seaweed and were easy to carry during a day trip.
Min visited Korea. His hosts offered a side dish of fermented cabbage and then cooked beef on a small grill at the table.
These were individual experiences, not rules about what everyone eats in each country.

E.title: An interview with a television cook
dialogue: Today we welcome television cook Daniel Wu. What dish would you recommend to beginners?
My favourite is a simple vegetable rice bowl. You can make it in about fifteen minutes.
Yes. Children can wash the vegetables, but an adult should use the hot pan.
Does it have to include chilli?
Not at all. The recipe is flexible: add chilli if you like spicy food, or replace it with fresh herbs.
No. Rice, carrots and eggs are affordable. It is also easy to make a meat-free version.
What is the most important thing for a beginner?
Prepare your ingredients before turning on the heat. That saves time and reduces mistakes.

F.title: Speaking model: food opinions
dialogue: Do you enjoy cooking at home?
Yes, especially on weekends. I often make vegetable soup because it is simple and healthy. I also like cooking with my sister because we can chat while preparing dinner.
Is there any food you dislike?
I am not keen on very oily food. It sometimes makes me feel uncomfortable, so I usually choose grilled or steamed dishes instead.
Do you prefer restaurants or home-cooked food?
I prefer home-cooked food most days because I know exactly what goes into the meal. However, I enjoy going to restaurants for special occasions.

G.title: Speaking Part 2 model: a memorable family meal
dialogue: I would like to talk about a family dinner that we had last summer. We celebrated my grandmother’s birthday at my uncle’s house. Around ten relatives came, including my cousins, so the atmosphere was cheerful.

The main dish was grilled fish with rice and fresh vegetables. My aunt prepared a light soup as well, and we all helped set the table. Before dinner, I cut fruit and arranged the plates. It was a simple meal, but everything tasted fresh.
What made the occasion special was not the food alone. My grandmother told us stories about her childhood, and my younger cousins asked lots of questions. We laughed and took a few photos together.

I enjoyed the dinner because our family members are usually busy, and we do not meet very often. That evening gave us time to talk without checking our phones. For me, it was a warm and memorable celebration.

items.question_vi: Điền mạo từ trước so sánh nhất.

activities.title: Approximate figures
activities.instruction_en: Use about, just over, just under or almost.
activities.instruction_vi: Dùng từ mô tả số xấp xỉ.

items.question_vi: 19 quán: gần 20.
items.explanation_en: 19 is slightly below 20.
items.explanation_vi: 19 thấp hơn 20 một chút.

items.question_vi: 35% so với một phần ba?
items.explanation_en: 35% is slightly over 33.3%.
items.explanation_vi: 35% cao hơn 33,3% một ít.

items.question_vi: 40 là chính xác hay xấp xỉ?
items.explanation_en: Do not approximate when the chart gives exactly 40.
items.explanation_vi: Khi biểu đồ ghi chính xác 40, không cần ước lượng.

activities.title: Explain trends using two time periods
activities.instruction_en: Describe beginning, middle and end.

items.question_en: How many cafés were there in 2016?
items.question_vi: 2016 có bao nhiêu quán chay?

items.explanation_vi: Cột đầu là 12.

items.question_vi: 2020 có mấy quán?
items.explanation_en: Middle bar shows 25.
items.explanation_vi: Cột giữa là 25.

items.question_vi: Tổng mức tăng 2016–2024?
items.explanation_en: 40 minus 12 equals 28.

activities.title: Avoid unsupported information
activities.instruction_en: Distinguish fact from unsupported inference.
activities.instruction_vi: Phân biệt thông tin số liệu và suy luận không có căn cứ.

items.question_en: “Local food had the largest share.” Supported?
items.question_vi: Local lớn nhất có được biểu đồ chứng minh?
items.explanation_en: It has 35%, the largest slice.
items.explanation_vi: Local 35% là lớn nhất.

items.question_en: “More cafés opened because everyone became vegetarian.” Supported?
items.question_vi: Tăng số quán do ai cũng ăn chay có bằng chứng?
items.explanation_en: No cause is displayed.
items.explanation_vi: Không có dữ liệu nguyên nhân.

items.question_en: “Café numbers rose throughout the period.” Supported?
items.question_vi: Số quán tăng liên tục có chứng cứ?
items.explanation_en: Each subsequent bar is taller.
items.explanation_vi: Mỗi cột sau cao hơn cột trước.

activities.title: Analyse an original model
activities.instruction_en: Find the introduction, overview and comparison.
activities.instruction_vi: Phân tích bài mẫu do English Skill Lab viết.

items.question_vi: Overview bắt đầu ở đoạn nào?
items.explanation_en: It begins with Overall and describes major patterns.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn 2 có Overall và ý chính.

items.question_en: Which paragraph gives the pie-chart percentages?

items.explanation_en: It compares 35%, 25%, 20%, 12% and 8%.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn 3 so sánh các phần trăm.

items.question_vi: Đoạn nào nêu mốc năm?
items.explanation_en: It reports numbers of cafés over time.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn 4 nêu số quán qua các năm.

activities.title: Prepare final exam task with two charts
activities.instruction_en: Write an overview and two comparisons from the 2019/2024 chart.
activities.instruction_vi: Lên overview và hai phép so sánh theo biểu đồ mới.

items.question_vi: Xu hướng chính là gì?
items.answer: All age groups became more likely to choose balanced meals.
items.explanation_en: Every 2024 bar exceeds its 2019 counterpart.
items.explanation_vi: Mọi cột 2024 cao hơn cột 2019.

items.question_vi: Nhóm cao nhất năm 2024?
items.explanation_en: The value is 69%, above other age groups.
items.explanation_vi: Nhóm 60+ đạt 69% cao nhất.

items.question_en: How many percentage points did the 45–59 group increase?
items.question_vi: Nhóm 45–59 tăng mấy điểm phần trăm?
items.explanation_en: 64% minus 55% is nine percentage points.
items.explanation_vi: 64 − 55 = 9 điểm phần trăm.

activities.title: Exam task: Task 1 (150+ words)
activities.instruction_en: Write at least 150 words from the exam chart within 20 minutes.
activities.instruction_vi: Viết tối thiểu 150 từ theo biểu đồ mới trong 20 phút.

items.question_en: Write a four-paragraph report (intro, overview, details 1 and 2).
items.question_vi: Viết 4 đoạn đúng bố cục.
items.answer: The chart compares the proportions of adults choosing balanced meals in four age groups in 2019 and 2024. Overall, all four groups saw increases.
items.explanation_en: The introduction states what is measured; the overview captures the main direction.
items.explanation_vi: Mở bài nêu dữ liệu; overview nêu xu hướng lớn.

items.question_en: Mention at least two comparisons with exact figures.
items.question_vi: Nêu ít nhất hai so sánh có số chính xác.
items.answer: The rate for adults aged 60+ rose from 61% to 69%, while the 18–29 group increased from 38% to 44%.
items.explanation_en: Use units correctly; figures represent percentages.
items.explanation_vi: Phải dùng đúng đơn vị phần trăm.

items.question_en: Check unsupported reasons or personal opinions.
items.question_vi: Kiểm tra không suy đoán nguyên nhân.
items.answer: Do not explain WHY diets changed; the chart does not report causes.
items.explanation_en: Task 1 is data description, not an opinion essay.
items.explanation_vi: Task 1 mô tả số liệu, không phải bài nêu quan điểm.

items.question_vi: Có quả cam nào không?
items.explanation_en: Any is usual in neutral questions.
items.explanation_vi: Câu hỏi trung tính thường dùng any.

items.question_vi: Chúng ta có ít bánh mì ăn sáng.
items.explanation_en: Bread is uncountable in this use.
items.explanation_vi: Bread không đếm được theo nghĩa này.

activities.title: Positive and negative food opinions
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track F. Extract one positive and one negative expression.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe Track F, tìm 1 cụm tích cực và 1 cụm tiêu cực.

items.question_vi: Cụm tích cực về nấu ăn
items.answer: I often make vegetable soup because it is simple and healthy.
items.explanation_en: Because introduces a reason.
items.explanation_vi: Because dùng để đưa lý do.

items.question_vi: Cụm thể hiện không thích đồ dầu mỡ
items.answer: I am not keen on very oily food.
items.explanation_en: Not keen on is a polite dislike.
items.explanation_vi: Not keen on là cách nói không thích tự nhiên, lịch sự.

items.question_vi: Cụm liên kết thể hiện đối lập
items.explanation_en: However introduces a different view.
items.explanation_vi: However mở ra ý kiến đối lập.

activities.title: Develop a Part 1 answer
activities.instruction_en: Use Answer → Reason → Example to speak for around 20 seconds.
activities.instruction_vi: Dùng Trả lời → Lý do → Ví dụ để nói khoảng 20 giây.

items.question_en: Do you prefer eating at home or going to restaurants?
items.question_vi: Bạn thích ăn ở nhà hay đi nhà hàng?
items.answer: I prefer eating at home because the food is usually fresher. For example, I can choose the amount of salt and vegetables in my meals.
items.explanation_en: A preference becomes stronger with a reason and example.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu sở thích kèm lý do và ví dụ làm câu trả lời đầy đủ.

items.question_en: Is there any food you avoid?
items.question_vi: Có món nào bạn tránh ăn không?
items.answer: I tend to avoid very sweet drinks because they make me thirsty. I usually choose plain water instead.
items.explanation_en: Avoid making medical claims; give personal preference.
items.explanation_vi: Chỉ nói sở thích cá nhân, tránh kết luận y khoa không cần thiết.

activities.title: Understand Speaking Part 2
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track G. Identify when, where, who, food and why special.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe Track G, xác định thời gian, nơi, người tham dự, món ăn và lý do đáng nhớ.

items.question_en: When did the event take place?
items.question_vi: Sự kiện diễn ra khi nào?
items.explanation_en: The talk starts with the time reference.
items.explanation_vi: Người nói nêu thời gian ở đầu bài.

items.question_vi: Buổi mừng diễn ra ở đâu?
items.explanation_en: The location is explicit.
items.explanation_vi: Địa điểm được nói trực tiếp.

items.question_vi: Đó là sinh nhật ai?
items.explanation_en: The candidate celebrated a grandmother’s birthday.
items.explanation_vi: Người nói mừng sinh nhật bà.

items.question_vi: Món chính nào được phục vụ?
items.explanation_en: The main dish is grilled fish with rice.
items.explanation_vi: Món chính là cá nướng với cơm.

items.question_vi: Vì sao đáng nhớ?
items.explanation_en: The candidate values rare time with family.
items.explanation_vi: Giá trị là thời gian hiếm hoi bên gia đình.

activities.title: Part 2 vocabulary bank
activities.instruction_en: Translate into natural English, not word-by-word.
activities.instruction_vi: Dịch sang tiếng Anh tự nhiên, không dịch từng chữ.

items.question_vi: Dịch: bữa ăn truyền thống
items.explanation_en: Traditional describes the type of meal.
items.explanation_vi: Traditional bổ nghĩa cho meal.

items.question_vi: Dịch: món ăn địa phương
items.explanation_en: Dish is a specific prepared food.
items.explanation_vi: Dish chỉ một món đã chế biến.

items.question_vi: Dịch: món nướng
items.explanation_en: Grilled describes the cooking method.
items.explanation_vi: Grilled chỉ phương pháp nướng.

items.question_vi: Dịch: món ăn đáng nhớ
items.explanation_en: Memorable means worth remembering.
items.explanation_vi: Memorable là đáng nhớ.

items.question_en: Translate: bầu không khí ấm áp
items.question_vi: Dịch: bầu không khí ấm áp
items.explanation_en: Warm can describe a friendly mood.
items.explanation_vi: Warm có thể mô tả bầu không khí thân mật.

activities.title: One-minute preparation
activities.instruction_en: Make keyword notes for food, place, people and reasons. No full sentences.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghi từ khóa theo món, nơi, người và lý do; không viết câu đầy đủ.

items.question_vi: Món ăn / nguyên liệu
items.explanation_en: Brief keywords are faster to review.
items.explanation_vi: Ghi từ khóa ngắn tiết kiệm thời gian.

items.question_vi: Địa điểm / thời gian
items.explanation_en: The notes should anchor a real event.
items.explanation_vi: Ghi rõ sự kiện cụ thể.

items.question_vi: Người tham dự và bầu không khí
items.explanation_en: Include people and feeling.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu người tham dự và cảm xúc.

items.question_vi: Vì sao đáng nhớ?
items.explanation_en: One strong reason is enough.
items.explanation_vi: Một lý do rõ là đủ phát triển bài nói.

activities.title: Two-minute response plan
activities.instruction_en: Use this structure: 20 sec intro; 40 sec scene; 40 sec details; 20 sec feeling.
activities.instruction_vi: Dùng cấu trúc: mở 20 giây; hoàn cảnh 40 giây; chi tiết 40 giây; cảm nhận 20 giây.

items.question_vi: Viết 1 câu mở đầu.
items.answer: I would like to talk about a meal I shared with my cousins last year.
items.explanation_en: Begin with the precise occasion.
items.explanation_vi: Mở bài nên nêu đúng sự kiện.

items.question_en: Write one sentence about the food.
items.question_vi: Viết 1 câu về món ăn.
items.answer: We cooked chicken noodles and served them with fresh vegetables.
items.explanation_en: Past simple recounts a completed occasion.
items.explanation_vi: Quá khứ đơn kể sự kiện đã xảy ra.

items.question_vi: Viết 1 câu kết.
items.answer: I still remember that meal because everyone helped and we had a great time.
items.explanation_en: The conclusion gives a personal reason.
items.explanation_vi: Kết bài cho lý do cá nhân.

activities.title: Introductions and conclusions
activities.instruction_en: Identify whether each sentence is intro (I) or conclusion (C).
activities.instruction_vi: Nhận diện câu là mở bài (I) hay kết bài (C).

items.question_en: I am going to describe a dish I first tried during a trip.
items.question_vi: Tôi sẽ mô tả món lần đầu thử trong chuyến đi.
items.explanation_en: It introduces the subject.
items.explanation_vi: Câu giới thiệu chủ đề.

items.question_en: That is why the experience has stayed in my memory.
items.question_vi: Đó là lý do trải nghiệm vẫn trong ký ức.
items.explanation_en: It closes the talk with reflection.
items.explanation_vi: Câu kết bằng suy ngẫm.

items.question_en: I would like to talk about a family celebration.
items.question_vi: Tôi muốn kể về dịp mừng của gia đình.
items.explanation_en: The listener knows what follows.
items.explanation_vi: Người nghe biết chủ đề tiếp theo.

items.question_en: Overall, it was a simple meal but a very special evening.
items.question_vi: Nhìn chung, bữa ăn đơn giản nhưng buổi tối đặc biệt.
items.explanation_en: It summarises the personal meaning.
items.explanation_vi: Câu tóm lại ý nghĩa cá nhân.

activities.title: Comparing planning notes
activities.instruction_en: Choose which notes would be easier to speak from.
activities.instruction_vi: Chọn dàn ý dễ sử dụng khi nói.

items.question_en: A. A full memorised paragraph B. Food / place / people / reason keywords
items.question_vi: A. Một đoạn thuộc lòng B. Từ khóa món/nơi/người/lý do
items.explanation_en: Part 2 planning time is short; keywords help natural speech.
items.explanation_vi: Thời gian chuẩn bị ngắn; từ khóa giúp nói tự nhiên.

items.question_en: A. Ten unrelated adjectives B. Three specific details and a personal reason
items.question_vi: A. 10 tính từ rời rạc B. 3 chi tiết cụ thể và 1 lý do
items.explanation_en: Specific content supports coherent development.
items.explanation_vi: Chi tiết cụ thể giúp phát triển mạch lạc.

items.question_en: A. Introduction, details, feelings B. Random facts with no order
items.question_vi: A. Mở - chi tiết - cảm xúc B. Thông tin ngẫu nhiên
items.explanation_en: A clear structure is easier to follow.
items.explanation_vi: Cấu trúc rõ dễ theo dõi.

activities.title: Speaking Part 2 exam simulation
activities.instruction_en: Describe a meal you enjoyed on a special occasion. Say: when/where, who was there, what you ate, why you remember it. Prepare 1 minute; speak up to 2 minutes.
activities.instruction_vi: Hãy kể một bữa ăn bạn rất thích trong dịp đặc biệt: khi nào/ở đâu, ai tham gia, ăn gì, vì sao đáng nhớ. Chuẩn bị 1 phút và nói tối đa 2 phút.

items.question_en: Plan four points (who, where, what, why).
items.question_vi: Lên dàn ý 4 điểm (ai, nơi, món, vì sao).
items.answer: family dinner; grandmother’s birthday; grilled fish; rare family time
items.explanation_en: Cover every cue card point with natural content.
items.explanation_vi: Bao quát mọi gợi ý trên thẻ, nội dung tự nhiên.

items.question_vi: Nói câu mở đầu phù hợp.
items.answer: I would like to describe a family dinner that I really enjoyed.
items.explanation_en: State the topic, not a memorised slogan.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu chủ đề, không dùng khẩu hiệu học thuộc.

items.question_vi: Nói câu kết có ý nghĩa.
items.answer: It was memorable because we were all together and had time to talk.
items.explanation_en: Close with why it mattered to you.
items.explanation_vi: Kết lại vì sao điều đó quan trọng với bạn.

writing_models.title: Task 1: Takeaway choices and vegetarian cafés
writing_models.text:
The pie chart shows the preferred takeaway cuisines in a survey, while the bar chart illustrates the number of vegetarian cafés in Brookfield from 2016 to 2024.

Overall, local dishes were the most popular takeaway option, whereas other cuisines accounted for the smallest share. The number of vegetarian cafés increased steadily across the period.

Local food represented 35% of the preferences, followed by Chinese cuisine at 25%. Italian dishes accounted for a fifth, while Indian food and other cuisines made up 12% and 8%, respectively. Together, local and Chinese food represented three fifths of all responses.

Regarding the number of cafés, there were 12 in 2016 and 19 in 2018. The figure rose to 25 in 2020, before reaching 34 in 2022 and 40 in 2024. The final number was therefore more than three times the initial figure.
writing_models.vi: Mở bài giới thiệu cả 2 biểu đồ. Overview nêu Local dishes nhiều nhất, Other ít nhất và số quán chay tăng đều. Thân bài 1 so sánh tỉ lệ, thân bài 2 trình bày biến động số quán theo mốc năm. Không tự giải thích nguyên nhân tăng.
